lines.t: Welcome back, my helper! The Duke's gold panels are finished. Now they need a safe room to stay in.
We are putting a new floor in the storeroom. Look around.
Hmm. We know the tiles and one side. Can the tiles tell us the other side?
Maybe! 56 is a lot of tiles.
Interesting. We'll have to check.
A square room? That would be tidy. Let's see.
Good. "Not sure yet" is a fine place to start.
One row across the room takes 7 tiles.
Let's find out how long the floor is.
576 inches? That is longer than this whole workshop.
Your times table is right, my friend. But is times the right thing to do here?
I think I see it. Do you?
Because you knew the area and one side, and you found the other side.
A border is not one plain rectangle. That is a puzzle for next time.
These are the new floor tiles for the storeroom.
Each tile is a square, 1 foot on every side.
My drawing of the storeroom floor.
One side is 7 feet. The other side has a question mark.

lines.t: Master Leonardo! I counted the tiles. There are 56. They will cover the whole floor, with none left over.
The storeroom is 7 feet wide. But crates block the far wall. I can't measure how long the room is!
Master Leonardo, the lid of the Duke's chest needs 72 gold sheets. One side is 8 inches. I found the other side!
But 72 times 8 is 576. I checked it twice!
Master Leonardo! The storeroom floor is done. Every tile fit, and not one was left over.
Now the Duke has a new wish. He sent a letter.
